favourable_outcome: the model predicts approval, that is the calibrated probability of approval at the requested amount reaches the cut-off
reference_population: the held-out test split of the dataset in question, 15 percent of the rows, never used for fitting, tuning, calibration or rule selection
reference_group_rule: the age group with the highest predicted approval rate

demographic_parity_ratio.source: four-fifths rule, EEOC 29 CFR 1607.4D - a convention from US employment law, used here as a warning line, not as a legal test under EU credit law

interval_method.resampling: test rows with replacement, not stratified by group, so group sizes vary as they would in a fresh sample
interval_method.covers: sampling variation in the test split only

verdict_rule: a metric is called within tolerance only when the whole interval sits inside it, and a breach only when all of it sits outside; otherwise undecided
